# /docs-update — the bounded human-doc review loop

Thin macro over the **already-coded** `tools.docs_guard` gate. Do NOT re-implement staleness
classification, digesting, coverage counting, or the drafting-exclusion set — the gate module
already encodes all four (DOCSUP-03/05), and `tools.docs_guard.exclusion_reason` is the single
tested classifier that says whether a target may be drafted into at all.

## Run the guard

`$ARGUMENTS` is passed **positionally** to the module — never interpolated into a constructed shell
string, and never assembled from registry, ledger or document content:

!`python -m tools.docs_guard $ARGUMENTS`

The module's own flags (`--registry`, `--ledger`, `--root`) are the only accepted extras. There is
no second data source: the guard is **re-run** here, always. Its report is the input, and a
regenerated staleness pointer is not — a pointer file is a derived, gitignored session convenience
that is simply absent in a fresh clone, so reading one instead of the guard would report "nothing to
do" on a clean checkout. That is a false green, not a clean tree.

## Routing table

| Exit | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| exit 0 | clean — no `BROKEN`, no `STALE_REQUIRED`, no failing coherence finding, uncovered within the ratchet | **STOP.** Nothing to do. `STALE_ADVISORY` blocks and warn/note findings appear on stderr and never change the code — do not chase them. |
| exit 1 | a `BROKEN` binding, a `STALE_REQUIRED` binding, a failing coherence finding, or an uncovered/binding-count regression | **The only working state.** For each enumerated binding, choose EITHER a bounded edit of that binding's target document OR the exact review disposition the report names, then route through `/review` and `/verify-work`. See `harness/skills/docs-upkeep/SKILL.md`. |
| exit 3 | the registry or the ledger is INVALID | **Refuse to draft anything.** This is a registry problem, not a documentation problem. Fix the malformed registry or ledger row and re-run. Editing a document here would be "fixing" the wrong artifact. |

Exit 2 is argparse's stdlib usage error and is never produced deliberately; treat it as a
mis-invocation of this command, not as a finding.

## What this command never does

- **Never restates contract drift or golden.** Those gates are **leading and authoritative**: this
  command does not re-run `contract_drift.run_gate()` and does not repeat its findings. A binding
  whose source is mid-drift renders as `SUPPRESSED (contract-drift leading)` and stops there — one
  change must not produce two failures with two different remedies.
- **Never widens the corpus.** `UNCOVERED` documents and the coverage ratchets are out of scope;
  raising a ratchet is a deliberate human edit.
- **Never authors a review-ledger row.** A binding is ratified by the human review commit that lands
  its reviewed row (ADR-0010 §3b) — an agent that could bless a binding has self-approved it.
- **Never drafts into an excluded target.** Ask `tools.docs_guard.exclusion_reason` rather than
  carrying a copy of the rule; the runtime write-side gates (`contract_guard`, the matrix path
  denies) are the backstop, not the decision.
